summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and tracheostomy was admitted for cough with green, blood-tinged sputum, throat pain, and inability to tolerate oral intake for two days. She had no fever, stable vital signs, and normal white blood cell count. Imaging showed no acute cardiopulmonary abnormalities, and ENT evaluation found no tracheal inflammation. A swallow study confirmed mild oropharyngeal dysphagia without aspiration, consistent with prior findings. She was managed symptomatically with pain control, dietary modifications, and continuation of home medications. She improved, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with instructions for soft diet, oral care, and follow-up with ENT and primary care.
